officialTitle: Cisplatin plus doxorubicin plus cyclophosphamide in metastatic or recurrent thymoma: final results of an intergroup trial
setting: Advanced (metastatic or locally progressive recurrent) thymoma

design.notes: Single-arm prospective cooperative-group (ECOG, SWOG, SECSG) trial; the abstract does not state the phase, recorded here as phase II by design type. Assessable patients: 29 thymoma and 1 thymic carcinoma, with metastatic or locally progressive recurrent disease after radiotherapy. Non-comparative evidence.

sponsor: Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group, Southwest Oncology Group, Southeastern Cancer Study Group
clinicalQuestion: What response and survival can be achieved with cisplatin, doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide (PAC) in advanced thymoma?

pico.population: Metastatic or locally progressive recurrent thymoma (one thymic carcinoma) after radiotherapy
pico.intervention: Cisplatin, doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide every 3 weeks for up to eight cycles
pico.outcomes: Response rate, duration of response, time to treatment failure, overall survival

arms.label: PAC
arms.dosing: Cisplatin 50 mg/m2, doxorubicin 50 mg/m2, cyclophosphamide 500 mg/m2 IV every 3 weeks, maximum eight cycles
arms.doseSourceQuote: were treated with intravenous cisplatin (50 mg/m2), doxorubicin (50 mg/m2), and cyclophosphamide (500 mg/m2) with normal saline hydration. Courses were repeated every 3 weeks for a maximum of eight cycles of therapy.

publications.title: Cisplatin plus doxorubicin plus cyclophosphamide in metastatic or recurrent thymoma: final results of an intergroup trial. The Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group, Southwest Oncology Group, and Southeastern Cancer Study Group.
publications.label: Final results

outcomes.sourceQuote: Three complete responses (CRs) and 12 partial responses (PRs) were observed (CR+PR rate, 50%; 95% confidence interval, 31.3% to 68.7%).
The median duration of response was 11.8 months (range, 0.9 to 70.5+)
the time to treatment failure 18.4 months (range, 0.8 to 91.9+)
and median survival time 37.7 months (range, 2 to 91.9+).

safety.description: Toxicity mainly haematological and mild; one episode of febrile neutropenia
safety.sourceQuote: Toxicity, which was primarily hematologic, was mild, with only one patient developing a fever associated with neutropenia.

strengths: Prospective multicentre cooperative-group trial in a rare tumour
limitations: Single-arm phase II-type evidence with a small sample; no comparator
Almost exclusively thymoma; minimal thymic carcinoma representation

clinicalImplications.text: Single-arm data supporting anthracycline-based cisplatin combination (PAC) as an active regimen in advanced thymoma; it remains a historical reference regimen given the absence of randomised trials.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Evidence in thymoma is single-arm: response rates across regimens are not directly comparable, and the PAC data come almost entirely from thymoma rather than thymic carcinoma.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 8201378. Arm n=30 = 29 thymoma + 1 thymic carcinoma assessable patients as printed. Phase not stated in abstract.
